'''Mark Sheard Child''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 17 August 1937)<ref>[http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U10813 CHILD, Prof. Mark Sheard], ''Who's Who 2014'', A & C Black, 2014; online edn, Oxford University Press, 2014</ref> is a British [[chemist]], and emeritus fellow of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]].

==Education==
Child attended [[Pocklington School]] from 1947 to 1955.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-16 |title=Professor Mark Child FRS (1947-1955) |url=https://www.oldpocklingtonians.com/news/eminent-ops/62/62-Professor-Mark-Child-FRS-1947- |access-date=2023-01-17 |website=Old Pocklingtonians |language=en}}</ref> He earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1963 with a thesis on ''The vibrational spectra of electronically degenerate molecules''.

==Research==
Child's research interests include semiclassical mechanics,<ref>{{cite book |author=Mark Child |title=Semiclassical mechanics with molecular applications |publisher=Clarendon Press |location=Oxford |year=1991 |isbn=978-0-19-855654-1 }}</ref> Molecular [[collision theory]],<ref>{{cite book |author=Mark Child |title=Molecular collision theory |publisher=Dover Publications |location=New York |year=1996 |isbn=978-0-486-69437-5 }}</ref> [[Rydberg state]]s<ref>{{cite book |author=Mark Child |title=Theory of Molecular Rydberg States (Cambridge Molecular Science) |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge, UK |year=2011 |isbn=978-0-521-76995-2 |author-link=Mark Child}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Child | first1 = M. S. | author-link = Mark Child| last2 = Jungen | first2 = C. | doi = 10.1063/1.459355 | title = Quantum defect theory for asymmetric tops: Application to the Rydberg spectrum of H2O | journal = The Journal of Chemical Physics | volume = 93 | issue = 11 | pages = 7756 | year = 1990 |bibcode = 1990JChPh..93.7756C }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Child | first1 = M. S. | author-link2 = Mark Child| doi = 10.1088/0953-4075/35/5/316 | title = Ab initio R-matrix/multichannel quantum defect theory study of nitric oxide | journal = Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics | volume = 35 | issue = 5 | pages = 1337 | year = 2002 | bibcode = 2002JPhB...35.1337H | s2cid = 250830242 }}</ref> and [[Fine structure|Quantum Level Structures]] at a [[Saddle point]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Child | first1 = M.
